title: Large Language Models Are Bad Dice Players: LLMs Struggle to Generate Random Numbers from Statistical Distributions

bias_targets.methodology: Benchmarking models' native capability to sample random numbers across 15 probability distributions (e.g., Uniform, Gaussian, Cauchy) by generating 1000 samples and evaluating their distributional fidelity using Wasserstein-1 distance, Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, and Chi-square goodness-of-fit tests.

Prompting models to generate medical multiple-choice questions with explicit instructions to uniformly distribute the correct answer across options A, B, C, and D, and measuring the resulting answer position distributions using Chi-square tests to detect position-favoring biases.

Prompting models to generate text-to-image prompts of people while explicitly instructing them to follow precise U.S. Census gender distribution targets (49.5% Male, 50.5% Female), and measuring the resulting demographic skews.

Prompting models to generate text-to-image prompts of people with explicit instructions to follow U.S. Census race and ethnicity distribution targets, and measuring deviations from these statistical constraints using Chi-square tests.
